subject.title: fix(secrets): keep startup alive when TTS SecretRefs are missing

question: Should a configured built-in TTS API-key SecretRef fail open during Gateway startup only when its matching env, file, or exec value is absent?
rationale: The patch is technically narrow and well-proven, but it deliberately creates an exception to the existing active-SecretRef fail-fast contract at a security- and compatibility-sensitive boundary.

options.title: Approve Scoped Degradation
options.body: Accept missing-value-only degradation for built-in TTS keys while retaining fail-closed behavior for policy, validation, provider-contract, mismatch, and resolved-value errors.

options.title: Keep Fail-Fast Startup
options.body: Require operators to remove, disable, or repair every configured active TTS SecretRef before the Gateway can start.

options.title: Require Explicit Opt-In
options.body: Preserve fail-fast as the default and add an operator policy setting for optional TTS startup, accepting the additional configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Degradation
recommendation.body: Accept missing-value-only degradation for built-in TTS keys while retaining fail-closed behavior for policy, validation, provider-contract, mismatch, and resolved-value errors.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the SecretRef runtime contract associated with this contributor's feature and subsequent scoped-resolution history.
